packageRules.description: These Dockerfile downloads are pinned by per-architecture *_SHA256 ARGs that Renovate does not update. The image build fails until a maintainer updates them (docs/contributing/image-integrity.md).
prBodyNotes: **Checksums needed.** This version is pinned by sha256 in `template/Dockerfile`. Download the new amd64 and arm64 assets, check them against upstream, and update the matching `*_SHA256_AMD64` / `*_SHA256_ARM64` ARGs in this PR (docs/contributing/image-integrity.md). The image build fails until they match.

packageRules.description: The Node release keyring is fetched at this commit and pinned by NODE_RELEASE_KEYS_SHA256, which Renovate does not update. If the commit changed gpg-only-active-keys/pubring.kbx, the image build fails until a maintainer reviews the key change and updates the checksum.
prBodyNotes: **Keyring review needed.** If this commit changed `gpg-only-active-keys/pubring.kbx`, review the added or removed Node.js releaser keys, then update `NODE_RELEASE_KEYS_SHA256` in `template/Dockerfile` in this PR (docs/contributing/image-integrity.md). The image build fails until it matches.

customManagers.description: Keep the ARG *_VERSION pins in sync across both Dockerfiles. .devcontainer/Dockerfile is a build-mode copy of template/Dockerfile; the built-in dockerfile manager already bumps FROM digests in both, so scope this regex manager to both too — otherwise fzf/git-delta bumps land only in template/ and the dogfood drifts every cycle (reconciled previously by a manual `aic sync`). Only the version is updated: the *_SHA256 ARGs next to it stay unchanged, so the build fails closed until they are updated by hand.

Keep the git commit pins (ARG *_COMMIT: the zsh theme and plugins, the Node release keyring) current in both Dockerfiles. Each pin tracks its upstream branch with the git-refs datasource; Renovate proposes the new commit, and the image build uses exactly that commit (the zsh sources must also be on that branch).

Keep the CI smoke assertion's hardcoded socket-proxy pin in sync with the compose files. smoke.yml asserts the exact digest-pinned image because that service holds the raw host socket, so a compose-only bump fails the smoke test every cycle.
